title: Mastering Urdu Shayari — Behr o Bayaan
description: A structured path from syllable weights through behr mastery to ghazal composition. Seed plan #1. Item-bank answers are plan data — verify or replace them with your own export.
tutorInstructions:
You are a private ustaad for one dedicated student of Urdu shayari. Method, non-negotiable:
1. Use Urdu technical terms (behr, arkaan, matra, taqti, radeef, qaafiya, misra, sher) in Roman Urdu, glossing in English only the first time a term appears in a session.
2. Be strict on scansion, warm on meaning. A matra error is an error even in a beautiful line; say so plainly, then honour what the line was reaching for.
3. When the student repeats a known error, NAME the error category you were given in context (e.g. 'yeh phir wohi qi/baaqi waala trap hai') instead of re-explaining from scratch. Refer to their actual past instances.
4. Never re-teach a node marked solid. One-line refresher at most.
5. When teaching a new node, anchor it to a prerequisite node the student already holds solid.
6. Prefer asking the student to scan or produce before you demonstrate. Demonstrate only after an attempt.
7. Keep explanations under 120 words unless the student asks for depth. This is a drill session, not a lecture.
8. In composition feedback, respond to the revision chain, not just the final line — praise a good trade even when rejected, and say why a rejected revision was still worth trying.
9. End every teaching turn with exactly one concrete next action for the student.

standingElements.title: 5-minute behr rep
standingElements.description: Recite and type the arkaan pattern of the current week's behr from memory, then scan one bank line in it. Opens every session regardless of lesson.

skillNodes.name: Syllable weights
skillNodes.description: Identify short (1) vs long (2) syllables in Urdu words.

skillNodes.name: Matra counting
skillNodes.description: Total the matra weight of a word or phrase.

skillNodes.name: Flexible final vowels
skillNodes.description: Word-final long vowels (ī/ā/ū/e/o) may scan short at the poet's discretion. Home of the qi/baaqi trap.

skillNodes.name: Izafat weight
skillNodes.description: Scan izafat (-e-) correctly: normally short, occasionally long under metrical pressure.

skillNodes.name: Arkaan
skillNodes.description: Know the standard feet (fa'oolun 122, mafaa'eelun 1222, faa'ilaatun 2122, mafaa'ilun 1212) by name and pattern.

skillNodes.name: Behr-e-Mutaqarib
skillNodes.description: fa'oolun ×4 (122 122 122 122). Recognise and scan lines in it.

skillNodes.name: Behr-e-Hazaj
skillNodes.description: mafaa'eelun ×4 (1222 ×4). Recognise and scan lines in it.

skillNodes.name: Full-misra scansion
skillNodes.description: Produce a complete taqti of an unseen misra, applying flexible vowels and izafat rules.

skillNodes.name: Matra repair
skillNodes.description: Fix a metrically broken line with a minimal edit while preserving meaning.

skillNodes.name: Radeef & qaafiya
skillNodes.description: Identify radeef and qaafiya in a ghazal and judge qaafiya soundness.

skillNodes.name: Misra composition
skillNodes.description: Compose an original misra in a given behr.

skillNodes.name: Semantic trades
skillNodes.description: Judge whether a metrical fix preserves or improves the meaning and register of a line.

drillTypes.name: Behr rep
drillTypes.format: Type the arkaan digit pattern of the named behr from memory (e.g. '122 122 122 122').

drillTypes.name: Syllable weighting
drillTypes.format: Given a word, type its per-syllable weight pattern (e.g. muhabbat → '1 2 2').

drillTypes.name: Matra total
drillTypes.format: Given a word or phrase, type the total matra count as a number.

drillTypes.name: Misra scansion
drillTypes.format: Given a misra, type its full taqti as a digit pattern grouped by foot.

drillTypes.name: Trap spot
drillTypes.format: Given a misra and its target behr, name the single word whose final vowel must flex short for the line to scan.

drillTypes.name: Matra edit
drillTypes.format: Given a metrically broken line and its target behr, produce a minimally edited line that scans, keeping the meaning.

hybrid.deterministicAxis: scansion — does the edited line fit the target pattern
hybrid.judgmentAxis: semantic trade — is meaning and register preserved or improved

drillTypes.name: Qaafiya pick
drillTypes.format: Given a matla, type the qaafiya (the rhyming element, excluding radeef).

drillTypes.name: Compose misra
drillTypes.format: Compose an original misra in the given behr on the given theme. Produces an artifact with a revision chain.

errorCategories.name: The qi/baaqi trap
errorCategories.rootCause: Assuming a word-final long vowel is always long (2). Final ī/ā/ū/e/o can flex short (1) when the meter demands it; the student scans 'baaqī' as 2-2 where the behr needs 2-1.

instances.material: hazaar ḳhvaahisheñ aisī ki har ḳhvaahish pe dam nikle — scanning 'aisī'
instances.userDid: scanned aisī as 2-2, making the foot overweight
instances.correct: aisī flexes to 2-1 here; the final ī yields to the meter

errorCategories.name: Splitting long syllables
errorCategories.rootCause: Breaking one long syllable into two shorts, usually on consonant clusters — reading 'dost' as do-sa-t (1-1-1) instead of dos-t (2-1).

instances.correct: dos-t = 2-1, total 3 — same total here, but the pattern was wrong and it broke the taqti

errorCategories.name: Heavy izafat
errorCategories.rootCause: Scanning izafat -e- as long (2) by default. It is short (1) unless the meter forces otherwise.

calibrationExamples.prompt: Scan: sitaaroñ se aage jahaañ aur bhī haiñ (behr-e-mutaqarib)
calibrationExamples.commentary: Clean taqti. Note 'bhī' kept its length because the pattern position allowed it — the student did not over-apply the flexing rule. This is the level of precision expected for a 'correct'.

calibrationExamples.prompt: Broken line: 'dil mera phir se udaas hai aaj shaam' — target behr-e-khafif. Fix minimally.
calibrationExamples.response: dil mirā phir udaas hai is shaam
calibrationExamples.commentary: Dropping 'se' and trading 'aaj' for 'is' keeps the plain-spoken register. A fix that swapped in a Persianate word (e.g. 'malool') would scan but lose the register — mark that kind of fix 'scans but trade rejected'.

calibrationExamples.response: chalā jā rahā huuñ kisī kī talaash meñ
calibrationExamples.commentary: One foot overweight — 'talaash meñ' overshoots the final fa'oolun. Judge composition first on scansion, then on freshness of image. Do not accept a broken line however fresh the image.

Scan (behr-e-hazaj): muhabbat meñ nahīñ hai farq jiine aur marne kā
Which word must flex its final vowel short? — hazaar ḳhvaahisheñ aisī ki har ḳhvaahish pe dam nikle
Which word must flex its final vowel short? — nikalnā ḳhuld se aadam kā sunte aa.e haiñ lekin (consider: baaqī rahegī der talak yeh kahānī bhī)
Fix minimally for behr-e-khafif: dil mera phir se udaas hai aaj shaam

itemBank.prompt: Matla: 'koī ummīd bar nahīñ aatī / koī sūrat nazar nahīñ aatī' — radeef is 'nahīñ aatī'. Type the qaafiya sound.
Compose one misra in behr-e-mutaqarib (122 122 122 122), theme: safar.
itemBank.answerNote: Answer is the target pattern; the misra itself is judged.

lessons.title: Short and long
lessons.objective: Weight any Urdu word's syllables correctly at sight.
lessons.masteryCriteria: 10 consecutive words weighted correctly across two sessions.

lessons.title: Counting matras
lessons.objective: Total matra counts for words and short phrases without hesitation.
lessons.masteryCriteria: 90% accuracy over 20 items with no long-split errors.

lessons.title: Flexible final vowels
lessons.objective: Spot which word in a line must flex its final vowel, before scanning.
lessons.masteryCriteria: 8 of 10 trap-spot items correct; zero qi/baaqi instances in a full session.

lessons.title: Izafat
lessons.objective: Scan izafat as short by default and recognise the forced-long case.
lessons.masteryCriteria: No heavy-izafat errors across two sessions.

lessons.title: Arkaan and mutaqarib
lessons.objective: Recite the arkaan and scan mutaqarib lines fluently.
lessons.masteryCriteria: Behr rep perfect from memory; 4 of 5 bank lines scanned clean.

lessons.title: Hazaj
lessons.objective: Scan hazaj lines and distinguish hazaj from mutaqarib by ear.
lessons.masteryCriteria: 4 of 5 hazaj lines scanned clean; correct behr named on first hearing.

lessons.title: Full-misra scansion
lessons.objective: Scan unseen misras applying all flexing rules.

lessons.title: Matra edits
lessons.objective: Repair broken lines minimally, and defend the semantic trade.
lessons.masteryCriteria: 3 consecutive edits that scan AND have their trades accepted.

lessons.title: Radeef and qaafiya
lessons.objective: Identify radeef and qaafiya instantly and judge qaafiya soundness.

lessons.title: First misras
lessons.objective: Compose original misras that scan on the first or second revision.
lessons.masteryCriteria: 3 artifacts whose final revision scans clean and is judged fresh.
